weighing.summary: One report of the time states a count for this hospital, 1,900 in all with 1,800 Union; the Union-only 1,800 is the same figure, not a rival. 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 have no source in the library or among the sites reached. Ranked by writing: a report written six weeks after the battle beats unsourced values; no better-ranked source disagrees.
weighing.who: J. H. Douglas was the Associate Secretary of the Sanitary Commission and writes to its General Secretary (Olmsted); he says he and six colleagues visited the hospitals. The 'Eleventh Corps hospital' is the Spangler farm's, not the XII Corps one (Bushman farm, 1,131 in the same table).
weighing.when: Report signed 15 Aug 1863, 42 days after the battle; the counts are not dated, and the writer does not say on which day the visits were made. A hospital's census changed day by day, so the figure is a count at an unstated date, not the number admitted or the number who died.
weighing.where: He was at the Gettysburg hospitals in the days after the battle (the text says the hospitals were visited by himself and others) and gives the figures as what he and the visitors saw or were told; the Confederate share is 'said to be'.
weighing.how_knew: Eyewitness visits and what the surgeons told him; he calls the figures 'approximative only, as that was all we sought for at the time', so the number is a rough census of wounded present, not a count of men admitted or treated.
weighing.clock: not applicable: a count, not a time.
weighing.independence: One group (Douglas). The National Park Service texts read (boundary study 1988, record of treatment, Common Pride and Fame) say the farm was the Eleventh Corps hospital but give no count. The Scott book names the hospital and gives no count. The 1,800 and 1,900 are one table. The value therefore carries the single_source flag; the project's working files that repeat 1,900 are leads and are not counted.

source_panel_text: About 1,900 wounded, 100 of them said to be Confederates: the Sanitary Commission's report of Aug 15, 1863 gives the Eleventh Corps hospital at the Spangler farm 1,900 (1,800 Union), as a rough count at an unstated date. The plan's 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 have no source found. All five values stay listed.
